correctness.rationale: Main lower-bound theorem M22(4,3)>=8 is fully proved by exact-rational enumeration. Independently re-executed inputs/artifacts/census.py: primary witness A*=[[3,3,0,0],[1,2,2,2],[2,0,2,2],[1,0,3,3]], B*=[[2,2,1,3],[0,2,3,0],[2,0,3,0],[1,1,0,2]] yields exactly 9 isolated square-support equilibria (1 pure [3],[3] with v=3,w=2; 8 with k=2 as tabulated), N22=8, all entries in {0..3}. Spot-checked indifference (e.g. I=[0,1],J=[1,2]: A-sub [[3,0],[2,2]] y=[2/3,1/3] gives v=2, outside rows 2/3 and 1 slack 4/3,1; B-sub [[2,1],[2,3]] x=[1/2,1/2] gives w=2, outside cols slack 1,1/2) and pure [3,3] strict slacks; all 8 rows have strictly positive mixtures with denominators 2-3, outside slacks >=1/3, extended (k+1)x(k+1) determinants +-2/+-3 nonzero, matching census_champion.json. Logic audited: M=[[A[I,J],-1],[1^T,0]], N=[[B[I,J]^T,-1],[1^T,0]] with Fraction Gaussian elimination, determinant-nonzero uniqueness, strict positivity and strict outside best-response; k=1 strict pure check; N top-left correctly uses B[I,J]^T. Fast integer screen count_N22_fast agrees with exact census on 1000 random {0..3} games (0 mismatches) and on all three witnesses. Secondary witness verified: total 9, N22=8. Bonus game verified: total 13 (4 pure+6 2x2+3 3x3), N22=6. 69-pair count correct (16+36+16+1). Alphabet containment verified. 1-step neighbourhood exhaustive (96 neighbours) max N22=8; 2-step exhaustive (9120 distinct) max 8, zero >=9, confirming local-optimality claim. Search-log arithmetic consistent (uniform hist 87185+12135+630+48+2=100000, total 101056 with hill evals; iterated totals sum to 516218). 4^32=2^64~=1.84e19 infeasibility statement correct. DRAFT honestly disclaims global upper bound (8<=M22<=36) and distinguishes proof (census) from heuristic saturation evidence. Minor imprecision: invoking continuum-total cap 15 for the slice via N22<=total needs nondegeneracy qualification (degenerate integer games not covered by the 15 bound), but stated conditionally and not part of certified lower-bound claim; does not falsify theorem.

originality.rationale: Nearest continuum prior art correctly cited and substantively distinct: (1) von Stengel 1999 DCG maximal numbers / Quint-Shubik counterexample family over real payoffs via polytope combinatorics - no bounded alphabet, no 2x2-slice maximum, no {0..3} witness; (2) Ickstadt-Theobald-von Stengel arXiv:2411.12385 / MOR 2025 stable-set bound settling n=5 at 31 and n=4 at 15 over nondegenerate real games via 159375 dual-neighborly polytope types - no integer-alphabet restriction, no M22(4,3), no exact-rational slack certificates; (3) von Stengel arXiv:2102.04580 exposition of Lemke-Howson/labeled polytopes/index-determinant machinery - method reference only, states no bounded-integer maximal-count result. Topic gap searches (arXiv/OpenAlex for bimatrix maximal numbers, support enumeration, integer-payoff enumeration) returned no bounded-alphabet 4x4 exact maximum; to auditor knowledge no textbook or paper pins M22(4,3) or a 2x2/3x3-slice enumeration with exact certificates. Failed-attempt and resultary scans cover disjoint objects. The integer-obstruction delta (which small determinants in {-6..6} and strict slacks with differences in {-3..3} can coexist across 36 pairs) is not present in continuum literature. Hence slice lower-bound witness with full census is substantively new, not a restatement; timestamp alone not relied upon.

value.rationale: Even taking correctness and novelty as given, the result is not independently worth finding later under SCOPE value standard. Object M22(4,3) (max number of isolated 2x2-support equilibria over {0..3} 4x4 games, excluding unequal supports and all degenerate ties) is an ad-hoc slice: no literature asks for the k=2 slice maximum at n=4,K=3; total-equilibrium maximum would be the natural quantity, and alphabet {0,1,2,3} has no theoretical justification (pilot used {0..5}, fallback bar >=6 arbitrary). Claim delivered is lower-bound-only existence of one matrix with 8 (upper bound openly 8..36, 15 only conditionally), with >2.8M heuristic games covering ~1.5e-13 of 1.8e19 space correctly disclaimed as non-proof, leaving no general theorem, no scaling family, no maximality insight. Per-equilibrium determinants/mixtures/slacks verify the example but do not explain it; structural note (only +-2/+-3 dets, uniform v=2, slacks 1/3-4/3) is explicitly non-proof observation on one example. Second witness (symmetric variant, same shape) and total-13 game add instances, not theory. Benchmark/learning motivation is generic and uninstantiated: no solver experiment, no Gambit/Game Theory Explorer comparison, no demonstration that this instance stresses algorithms beyond random games. This is therefore an unexplained brute-force table plus arbitrary-parameter instance plus first lower bound on an invented quantity - the class SCOPE explicitly rejects (textbook-adjacent enumeration, mere parameter substitution K=3, tiny unmotivated gain, unexplained enumeration) even if correct and new, analogous to the rejected narrow RT(30,K4,6) instance. Exceeding the pre-registered >=6 bar does not create independent value.
